docs.title: Development of simple Flexray Driver
docs.text:
2021 — Daimler Central Gateway Project

Tags: FlexRay, Embedded C, Interrupt/Polling, CEIC

Implemented an optimized Flexray Driver for driving one specific Flexray controller, enabling only one channel with a limited number of configured frames This was needed to enable Flexray communication in a particular project with as minimal memory footprint as possible with as fast run-time as possible This bare metal Flexray driver did not follow AUTOSAR standards, dint implement all AUTOSAR APIs, dint use joblist or interrupts and is not reusable as-is in other projects (That's the way it was intended to be developed)

docs.title: Unified Modeling Language - Basics
docs.text:
Sep-2024

Tags: Modeling, Requirements Engineering, Use Case Diagrams, Activity Diagrams, Domain Modeling, Component Diagrams, Sequence Diagrams, State Diagrams

Notes from a UML basics course, covering how UML is used to model software across requirements, architecture and detailed design. On the requirements side: use case diagrams, activity diagrams for each scenario of a use case (positive, negative, error), and a domain model built with class diagrams in the customer's own vocabulary. On the architecture side: component diagrams (ports, interfaces, composites) for the static view, sequence diagrams for runtime behaviour, and state diagrams for states and their transitions.

docs.title: Software Architecture - Basics-B (foundation for CPSA-F certification)
docs.text:
May-2025

Tags: Architecture Design, Impact Factor Analysis, SOLID Principles, Architecture Views, Architectural Patterns, Hexagonal Architecture, Design Principles, Design Patterns

Notes from a software architecture foundation course preparing for the iSAQB CPSA-F certification. Topics: what architecture is, its building blocks and goals, and why it is shaped more by quality requirements than by functional ones; analysis with use cases and domain models; identifying and analysing the factors that most affect architectural decisions; design approaches (top-down, bottom-up, upfront, emergent, iterative); design principles (loose coupling, strong cohesion, open-closed, information hiding); architecture views (context, building block, runtime, deployment); and architectural patterns (layers, ports and adapters, pipes and filters, microservices, blackboard).

docs.title: Cybersecurity Best Practices
docs.text:
Feb-2026

Tags: Cybersecurity, Security Frameworks, Defense in Depth, Network Security, Case Study

Notes from Coursera's Cybersecurity Best Practices: a recap of the CIA triad; a Maersk case study showing a security programme run as risk assessment → framework selection → gap assessment → roadmap; an overview of the main security frameworks and standards (NIST CSF, CIS Controls, ISO/IEC 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA Security Rule, OWASP Top Ten, SANS); and the basics of securing a network through segmentation, VLANs, subnets and access control rules.

docs.title: Introduction to Cybersecurity Fundamentals
docs.text:
Feb-2026

Tags: Cybersecurity, Security Fundamentals, Incident Response, Data Protection, Social Engineering

Notes from Coursera's Introduction to Cybersecurity Fundamentals. Topics covered: the core security properties (authentication, authorization, non-repudiation, integrity, confidentiality, availability); the main types of attack and the psychology behind phishing, malware, ransomware and social engineering; risk mitigation and authentication best practices; how data is classified, protected and disposed of; and the stages of incident response.
